stem: Researchers isolate nucleic acids from cultured fibroblasts and incubate them with latex beads linked to short sequences of repeated thymidine residues.  The beads are then washed to remove unbound nucleic acids.  A specific nucleic acid sequence is found to bind preferentially to the residues attached to the beads.  This sequence is most likely present in which of the following?​‌​‌‌​‌‌​​​​​‌​​​​​‌‌‌‌‌​‌​‌‌​‌‌​‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌​​‌​‌​​‌‌​‌‌​​‌‌‌​‌‌‌​​​‌​​‌‌​‌‌‌​‌‌​‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌​​‌​‌‌‌​​‌​​‌​‌‌‌​‌​‌‌‌​‌​‌​‌‌​‌​‌​​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​​​​‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌​‌‌‌​​​​​​​‌​‌‌​​‌​‌‌​​‌​​‌​‌​​​‌​​​​​​‌‌​​‌‌‌​​​‌‌​​​‌‌‌​​​​‌​‌‌​‌‌‌​​​​‌‌​‌‌​‌‌​​​​‌​​​‌​​​​​‌​​‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌​​​​​‌‌​​​​​‌​‌‌​​‌​​‌​​‌​‌‌​​​​‌​​​‌​​​‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌​​​‌‌‌​​‌​​​‌​​​‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌‌
explanation:
In this experiment, beads linked to short sequences of repeated thymidine residues selectively bind nucleic acids containing repeated adenine residues through complementary base pairing.  Such sequences are found in the poly(A) tail at the 3′ end of most mature eukaryotic mRNAs.

During eukaryotic gene expression, pre-mRNA undergoes processing in the nucleus to form mature mRNA.  This includes removal of introns by splicing and addition of a 5′ 7-methylguanosine cap and a 3′ poly(A) tail.

The poly(A) tail is a chain of adenine-containing ribonucleotides, typically about 200–250 nucleotides long when first synthesized.  Polyadenylation involves recognition of a signal sequence (usually AAUAAA) and cleavage of the RNA downstream of this signal.  Poly(A) polymerase then adds adenine nucleotides to the newly formed 3′ end without requiring a template.  The tail facilitates nuclear export, protects mRNA from degradation, and promotes translation.  Over time, progressive shortening of the tail reduces this protection, promoting mRNA breakdown.

(Choice B)  The anticodon of tRNA is a 3-nucleotide sequence that pairs with a complementary mRNA codon during translation.  Although an anticodon can contain 3 adenine residues, this short sequence cannot form as extensive or stable a hybrid with the bead-bound thymidine sequences as a poly(A) tail.

(Choice C)  DNA promoter regions contain regulatory sequences (eg, TATA and CAAT boxes) that bind transcription factors to help initiate transcription.  These sequences lack long stretches of consecutive adenine residues and therefore would not bind efficiently to the beads.

(Choice D)  Pre-mRNA contains exons, which are retained in mature mRNA, and introns, which are removed by splicing.  Spliceosomes recognize splice sites that typically contain GU at the 5′ end of an intron and AG at the 3′ end.  These sequences are not complementary to repeated thymidine residues.

(Choice E)  Telomeres help maintain chromosomal stability and consist of repetitive DNA at chromosome ends.  Human telomeric repeats (TTAGGG and the complementary sequence CCCTAA) lack long stretches of consecutive adenine residues and therefore would not bind efficiently to the beads.

Educational objective:The poly(A) tail at the 3′ end of most mature eukaryotic mRNAs facilitates nuclear export, protects against degradation, and promotes translation.  Its repeated adenine residues enable stable binding to sequences of repeated thymidine residues through complementary base pairing.​‌​‌‌​‌‌​​​​​‌​​​​​‌‌‌‌‌​‌​‌‌​‌‌​‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌​​‌​‌​​‌‌​‌‌​​‌‌‌​‌‌‌​​​‌​​‌‌​‌‌‌​‌‌​‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌​​‌​‌‌‌​​‌​​‌​‌‌‌​‌​‌‌‌​‌​‌​‌‌​‌​‌​​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​​​​‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌​‌‌‌​​​​​​​‌​‌‌​​‌​‌‌​​‌​​‌​‌​​​‌​​​​​​‌‌​​‌‌‌​​​‌‌​​​‌‌‌​​​​‌​‌‌​‌‌‌​​​​‌‌​‌‌​‌‌​​​​‌​​​‌​​​​​‌​​‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌​​​​​‌‌​​​​​‌​‌‌​​‌​​‌​​‌​‌‌​​​​‌​​​‌​​​‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌​​​‌‌‌​​‌​​​‌​​​‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌‌
